state.case_summary: A 17-year-old nulliparous female presented with a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension. She initially sought evaluation for bloating but was advised to diet for presumed weight gain. She denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history of cancer. On examination, her BMI was 20.5 kg/m2, blood pressure 125/85 mmHg, pulse 89/min, and SpO2 95% on room air. The abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus. Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor. Laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL); APTT, INR, electrolytes, urea, and creatinine were normal. Tumor markers included HE4 69.1 pmol/L (N ≤ 60.5), LDH 202 U/L (N ≤ 48.5), with alpha-fetoprotein 4.54 ng/mL (N ≤ 5.8), CA-125 23.1 U/mL (N ≤ 35), and β-hCG <0.2 mIU/mL all within normal limits. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava. The lesion appeared unilocular with a 1.5 mm wall and no septations or solid components, and was suggestive of an ovarian origin.

root.label: Chronic Progressive Abdominal Distension with Palpable Mass and Ovarian Tumor
